args.question: What is the threshold for "quality metric is too low"? Should I use sigstrdb (signal strength in dB) as the quality metric, and if so, what value defines "too low"? For example, should signals with sigstrdb < -150 be marked as 'Weak'?

result: The quality metric is determined by the Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI), which is calculated as `SnrRatio - 0.1 * ABS(NoiseFloorDbm)`. Signals are considered to have a "too low" quality if this SNQI value is less than 0.

content: What is the threshold for "quality metric is too low"? Should I use sigstrdb (signal strength in dB) as the quality metric, and if so, what value defines "too low"? For example, should signals with sigstrdb < -150 be marked as 'Weak'?

args.sql: SELECT signalregistry, snrratio, noisefloordbm, snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(noisefloordbm) AS snqi FROM signals WHERE snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(noisefloordbm) < 0 LIMIT 10;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signals WHERE snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(noisefloordbm) < 0;
UPDATE signals SET signalclass = 'Weak' WHERE snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(noisefloordbm) < 0;
